what: Exercise 3: IPD Model Fitting via the Chen & Chen Estimator
title: Unit 00: Getting Started
text: Let us run one method, chen (‘Chen & Chen’ estimator proposed Gronsbell et al., 2025). Chen & Chen estimator IPD method combines information : Labeled data (true outcome, YY, model predictions, ff, available), Unlabeled data (model predictions, ff, available). Rather treating every unlabeled observation equally, applies data-driven weight, $\hat{W}^{\rm CC}$, unlabeled contribution obtains $$ \hat{\beta}^{\rm CC} = \hat{\beta}^{\rm lab} - \hat{W}^{\rm CC}(\hat{\gamma}^{\rm lab} - \hat{\gamma}^{\rm }) $$ $\hat{\beta}^{\rm lab}$ slope estimate classical regression, $\hat{\gamma}^{\rm lab}$ slope estimate naive regression labeled data, $\hat{\gamma}^{\rm }$ slope estimate naive regression labeled + unlabeled data, $\hat{W}^{\rm CC}$ reflects amound additional information carried predictions. adaptively weighting unlabeled information, Chen & Chen estimator achieves greater precision using labeled data alone, without sacrificing validity, even predictions imperfect. Let’s call method using ipd() function collect estimate slope X1 linear regression (model = "ols"): ipd_model S4 object slots things like coefficient, se, ci, coefTable, fit, formula, data_l, data_u, method, model, intercept. can extract coefficient table using ipd’s tidy helper compare naive classical methods:

Error` = c(naive_df$std.error, classical_df$std.error, ipd_df$std.error) )  compare_tab #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   Method    Estimate `Std. what: 3 Model Training on the Training Set
title: Unit 01: The Rashoman Quartet
text: , fit four predictive models using entire 1,000-row train dataset (ignoring dataset column): Decision Tree via ctree() (max depth = 3, minsplit = 250). Linear Regression via lm(). Random Forest via randomForest() (100 trees). Neural Network via neuralnet() (two hidden layers: 8 units, 4 units; threshold = 0.05). evaluate model’s performance full 1,000-row test set using DALEX extract R2R^2 RMSE. Interpretation: four models (Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Neural Network) deliver essentially identical predictive performance test set: R2≈0.7290,RMSE≈0.3535. R^2 \approx 0.7290,\quad \mathrm{RMSE} \approx 0.3535.
code: set.seed(1568)  # 1) Decision Tree (ctree) model_dt <- ctree(   formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,   data    = train,   control = ctree_control(maxdepth = 3, minsplit = 250) ) exp_dt <- DALEX::explain(   model   = model_dt,   data    = test %>% select(x1, x2, x3),   y       = test$y,   verbose = FALSE,   label   = "Decision Tree" ) mp_dt <- model_performance(exp_dt)  # 2) Linear Regression model_lm <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = train) exp_lm <- DALEX::explain(   model   = model_lm,   data    = test %>% select(x1, x2, x3),   y       = test$y,   verbose = FALSE,   label   = "Linear Regression" ) mp_lm <- model_performance(exp_lm)  # title: Unit 03: BCR-ABL Fusion in B-Cell Leukemia
text: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia () common childhood cancer, exhibits marked genetic heterogeneity, distinct chromosomal translocations defining molecular subtypes divergent prognoses therapeutic responses. B-cell lineage , BCR-ABL1 fusion (“breakpoint cluster region”/“Abelson”, .e., “Philadelphia chromosome”) arises t(9;22) translocation encodes constitutively active tyrosine kinase. fusion historically associated poor outcomes, advent targeted therapies (e.g., imatinib) revolutionized treatment survival. High-density microarray profiling measures expression 7,000 genes leukemic blast cells, enabling form “molecular diagnostics” supervised learning can: Classify fusion status genetic subtypes cytogenetic assays (PCR, FISH) unavailable. Discover novel marker genes pathways dysregulated specific fusions. Predict therapeutic response stratify risk using expression-derived scores. However, many retrospective multi-center cohorts, subset patients undergo gold-standard fusion testing (e.g., RT-PCR BCR-ABL1), leaving majority “unlabeled.” common workaround train gene expression classifier small labeled subset apply larger unlabeled cohort. Yet, naive downstream analyses, treating predicted labels ground truth, can yield biased effect estimates understate uncertainty. Inference Predicted Data (IPD) offers principled remedy: combines small labeled set predicted labels (e.g., true fusion status) larger unlabeled set, adjusting bias variance. module, : Describe Golub Bioconductor datasets. Subset data B-cell filter top 500 variable probes. Harmonize probes across platforms via gene symbols. Split data train three classifiers BCR-ABL1 fusion status. Predict holdout Golub B-cell data using -trained classifier. Apply IPD estimate association fusion status patient sex assigned birth. end, understand leverage expression-based predictions maintaining valid inference genetic subtypes cohorts partially missing gold-standard labels. Note: data loading prediction workflows, directly follow Bioconductor MLInterfaces vignette VJ Carey P Atieno: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/MLInterfaces/inst/doc/MLprac2_2.html

code: # Load the ALL data data(ALL)  # Subset ALL to B-cell lineage (BT codes starting with "B") bALL <- ALL[, substr(pData(ALL)$BT, 1, 1) == "B"]  # Keep only fusion-negative ("NEG") and fusion-positive ("BCR/ABL") samples fus <- bALL[, bALL$mol.biol %in% c("NEG", "BCR/ABL")]  # Convert to factor with clear levels: NEG=0, BCR/ABL=1 fus$mol.biol <- factor(fus$mol.biol, levels = c("NEG", "BCR/ABL"))  # Compute median absolute deviation (MAD) for each probe devs <- apply(exprs(fus), 1, mad)  # Select top 500 most variable probes by MAD ranking top500 <- order(devs, decreasing = TRUE)[1:500]  # Subset ExpressionSet to top 500 probes dat_filt <- fus[top500, ]  # Confirm dimensions: 500 probes x n samples dim(exprs(dat_filt)) #> [1] 500  79
